script: In 1957, the Soviets needed to beat America into space again, but they only had four weeks to build a new spacecraft. So they grabbed a stray dog off the streets of Moscow named Laika, and trained her to sit still inside a tiny capsule. There was a secret nobody told the public: the ship was never designed to bring her back. Engineers built her a pressurized cabin, monitored her heartbeat, and launched her aboard Sputnik 2, making her the first living creature to orbit the Earth. For decades, the Soviet Union claimed she died peacefully days later. The truth stayed hidden for over forty years. She had actually died from overheating just hours after launch. Laika never came home, but she proved a living creature could survive the launch into space.
